summary: Feed s136_double is degraded for APM: 8.0% duplicate packets and 69.4% one-way TCP sessions (111/160) prevent bidirectional transaction correlation.

findings.root_cause: 8.0% duplicates (148/1850) indicates overlapping SPAN/TAP sources or packet broker forwarding the same packet via two paths without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will double-count transactions, inflate throughput and latency metrics, and waste 10G tool capacity on redundant packets, distorting application performance analysis.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication with a 5-10ms window to drop identical packets arriving via duplicate paths before delivery to the APM.

findings.root_cause: 69.4% of TCP sessions show only one direction, indicating asymmetric routing or broker aggregation/load-balancing that splits client->server and server->client to different tool ports, so this APM feed receives only one side.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to pair requests with responses and measure response time/error rate; one-way visibility breaks transaction correlation, latency calculation, and dependency mapping for 111 of 160 sessions.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same APM tool port using symmetric hashing, restoring complete bidirectional visibility required for APM.
